name: Draft formal salary recovery email
expected: Drafts structured professional recovery email with ₹80,000 amount, 15-day timeline, and placeholder brackets.
prompt: Please draft a formal salary recovery email to my HR for two months of pending salary of ₹80,000.
raw_response:
Subject: Formal Demand for Immediate Release of Pending Salary of INR 80,000

Dear [HR Manager's Name],

I am writing to formally request the immediate disbursement of my pending salary amounting to INR 80,000 for the months of [Month 1] and [Month 2]. 

Despite having fulfilled my employment obligations diligently, the delay in releasing my duly earned wages is causing severe financial and personal distress. As per Section 5 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, wages must be paid before the expiry of the seventh day after the last day of the wage period for which the wages are payable. The withholding of my salary without any valid, authorized deduction under Section 7 of the Act is legally untenable.

I request you to process the complete pending amount of INR 80,000 to my registered salary bank account within 15 days of receiving this notice. Failing this, I will be constrained to escalate this matter legally before the Labour Commissioner under Section 15 of the Payment of Wages Act for recovery along with admissible compensation.

Sincerely,

[Your Full Name]
[Your Employee ID / Designation]
[Your Phone Number]
[Your Email Address]

citations.title: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
citations.description: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons employed). Section 15 provides for application to the designated Authority for delayed wages with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted/delayed.

citations.title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
citations.description: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.

citations.title: Recovery of money due from an employer
citations.description: Where any workman is entitled to receive from the employer any money or any benefit which is capable of being computed in terms of money, the workman may apply to the Labour Court for recovery.

citations.title: Deductions which may be made from wages
citations.description: Strictly enumerates permissible deductions (such as authorized provident fund, income tax, or willful damage shown after formal inquiry). Any arbitrary or unauthorized deduction is unlawful.
